Apple nearly a year ago was found to have infringed on a Masimo patent related to low-power blood oxygen measurement in the Apple Watch.

At the time, Apple was ordered to pay $634 million, but a federal judge has now ordered an additional $184 million...

Apple has been fighting Masimo, the medical technology company, on multiple fronts. One significant case involved the International Trade Commission ruling in 2023 that Apple must remove the blood oxygen feature from two Apple Watch models in order to continue selling them in the United States. The Cupertino-based company was forced to redesign how the feature works in order to be permitted to bring the devices to the U.S. market.

But Apple was also facing a lawsuit from Masimo seeking damages for Apple's use of its patented method of measuring blood oxygen in a low-power manner. Apple was found to have infringed on the patent and ordered to pay an amount equal to the patent licensing fees it should have paid.

According to Bloomberg Law, Apple has now been ordered to pay an additional $184 million in interest on that amount.

There is some good news for Apple. Masimo sought interest calculated at 7 percent, but the judge rejected that request, ruling that the rate should be equivalent to what Masimo itself pays to borrow. However, with interest compounding annually, the total amount still grew by an additional $184 million.
